transcript:
Header:
- Date/Time: 2026-09-30 15:00 PT
- Duration: ~42 minutes
- Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Rachel Kim (FinEdge Head of ML), Marcus Lee (FinEdge Platform Eng), Priya Nair (FinEdge Security), Tom O'Hara (FinEdge PM)

Summary (auto): Discussed rollout strategy: runbook steps for canary, monitoring signals (latency, p99/p95, error rates, hallucination/regression checks), traffic split for A/B test, cutover and rollback criteria, and outstanding security/compliance gating items.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samira (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call - can you confirm we have Rachel, Marcus, Priya, Tom?
[00:08] Rachel (FinEdge): Yep, here.
[00:11] Marcus: Marcus here.
[00:12] Priya: Present.
[00:13] Tom: Here.
[00:15] Samira: Great. High level for today - finalize canary/cutover approach and agree next steps for the go-live checklist. Diego, you want to run the technical plan?
[00:25] Diego (Redwood SE): Sure - I'll walk through the canary flow we recommend and the monitoring hooks. Quick caveat: some of the metric names in our demo dashboards are shorthand; we'll send exact Grafana links after this.
[00:36] Diego: Step 1, deploy canary endpoints on Redwood Dedicated pool with the same model/version as prod. Step 2, route 1-5% of production traffic for 24 hours, depending on QPS. Step 3, monitor latency p95/p99, error rate, token throughput, and business-level quality signals - e.g., hallucination rate measured against a small labeled prompt set. Step 4, if stable, increase to 20-30% over next 24-48 hours, then full cutover with blue/green or weighted A/B.
[01:10] Rachel: For our usage pattern, latency is a hard SLO - p95 under 400ms for single-turn gen - and cost is a big factor. Are you able to show how the cost delta looks between hosted and dedicated?
[01:21] Samira: Yes, we'll include the cost delta in the pricing doc - we already shared an initial spreadsheet but we'll update it with expected unit economics for the canary traffic mix and batching gains.
[01:31] Marcus: On traffic, our endpoints are roughly 120 QPS at peak across 3 routes; mean tokens per request is about 90. We'll send the time-of-day distribution. That influences how aggressive the canary can be.
[01:45] Diego: Good, that 90 token average is useful. For 120 QPS we recommend starting at 1% (so ~1.2 QPS) to validate correctness and tracing, then if stable go to 10-15% to stress autoscaling and batching.
[01:58] Tom: Question about rollout method - we're leaning to A/B for model comparison vs blue/green for infra. Any recommendation?
[02:06] Diego: If the goal is to compare model quality, A/B is best - split traffic at the routing layer and compare outputs against your labeled prompts. For infra/ops safety, blue/green or weighted rollout is safer: you can switch 100% quickly. Often teams do A/B for 48 hours for quality checks, then blue/green for final cutover.
[02:25] Priya: From security side, we need SSO, audit logs, KMS integration, and a signed SOC2 addendum before full production. Are those in place?
[02:34] Samira: Yes - SSO/SAML and RBAC are available. We can share the SOC2 whitepaper and our KMS integration guide; Diego will attach the audit log retention options and exact log endpoints. We did note that for Private deployments we can set customer-managed KMS - for Dedicated we have an integration pattern.
[02:54] Priya: Perfect. Also, we need to know where logs live - can we ship golden alerts to our existing PagerDuty and create a read-only Grafana view?
[03:02] Diego: Absolutely - we support webhook/Prometheus alertmanager and can provision a read-only Grafana dashboard with special dashboards for canary metrics. We'll include those links in the runbook.
[03:12] Rachel: On quality monitoring - you mentioned a labeled prompt set to detect regressions. How are you recommending we measure hallucination and semantic drift?
[03:21] Diego: For the POC we recommend a two-track approach: automated checks on the labeled set for precision/recall style metrics, and human review on a sample of 100 responses per day for the first week. We'll supply the eval harness and the scripts to run comparisons.
[03:36] Tom: If we see a quality delta beyond the tolerance, what's the rollback plan?
[03:40] Diego: Rollback is straightforward: for A/B you can redirect traffic back to the control model. For blue/green, flip to the previous environment. We'll codify thresholds in the runbook, e.g., >5% increase in hallucination rate or >2x error rate triggers rollback. Those numbers are configurable and we want your input.
[03:58] Rachel: 5% hallucination seems high. Can we tighten to 2% for critical endpoints?
[04:03] Samira: We can make endpoint-specific thresholds. We'll make the runbook accept parameterized thresholds per route.
[04:09] Marcus: I want to make sure autoscaling behaves - can you call out warmup time, queue sizes, and KV cache warm state? We saw a cold-start p95 jump in the early tests.
[04:19] Diego: Yes - warmup varies by model and GPU type. For your workload, we're seeing cold-start p95 at ~1.2s and warm p95 ~320ms on Dedicated; that's with continuous batching and KV cache. We'll include pre-warm hooks and suggest keeping a small baseline reserved capacity during rollout to avoid cold starts.
[04:38] Samira: Also note we have a burst policy option - you can allow short spikes above committed capacity with a rate-limited fallthrough to hosted fallback if Dedicated is fully saturated.
[04:48] Tom: Fallback to hosted - is data separation and privacy preserved during fallback? That's a blocker for us - some flows are regulated.
[04:56] Samira: Good call - we can configure routing policies to never fallback for regulated routes. Or for Private/VPC deploys fallback is disabled. We'll put that in the policy docs.
[05:05] Priya: For audit, do you retain request/response payloads by default? We need to avoid storing PHI and have retention rules.
[05:13] Diego: By default we store telemetry and metadata; raw payload retention is configurable. We can redact or route those to your S3 with lifecycle policies. We'll send the configuration options.
[05:22] Marcus: Back to cutover - what's the recommended timeline? We're targeting a weekend low-traffic window in mid-October.
[05:30] Samira: That's reasonable. Here's a suggested timeline: 1) Prep & security sign-off (this week), 2) Canary (1-3 days), 3) Extended A/B for quality (48-72 hours), 4) Blue/green final cutover during low-traffic window, 5) Post-cutover 72-hour monitoring. We can compress but we should respect the cooldown windows.
[05:52] Rachel: For the canary, do you need a synthetic traffic harness or will real production traffic be used?
[05:58] Diego: Prefer real traffic for quality signals; synthetic can supplement to exercise edge cases or load. If you want to limit exposure, start with synthetic for initial latency/stress then move to 1% real traffic.
[06:09] Tom: Monitoring - can you list the exact signals you recommend we track during canary?
[06:14] Diego: Sure - p50/p95/p99 latency, server error rate (5xx), model error rate (timeouts, truncated responses), token throughput, queue length, GPU utilization, model quality metrics (hallucination, response similarity), and business KPIs like conversion rate if applicable. We'll add spike detection and drift alerts.
[06:34] Priya: We also want anomaly detection on a per-tenant basis since different customers have different behavior. Can your dashboards scope by tenant?
[06:40] Diego: Yes - we tag requests with tenant ID and have per-tenant panels. We can configure alerts scoped to tenant thresholds.
[06:47] Samira: A quick note about rollout safety: we'll provide feature-flag integrations so you can rapidly throttle or disable new model routes via your existing control plane. That buys a lot of safety during the 48-72 hour window.
[06:59] Marcus: Regarding the runbook, can you outline the top-level steps now so we capture them in the meeting notes?
[07:04] Diego: Top-level runbook: Pre-checks (security, infra, backup), deploy canary instance, redirect 1% traffic + synthetic validation, monitoring baseline for 24h, expand to 10-30% depending on stability, A/B analysis for 48h (quality), final cutover via blue/green with DNS/feature flag swap, post-cut 72h watch, rollback if thresholds breached.
[07:26] Tom: Who's on-call during canary? We need an escalation matrix.
[07:30] Samira: We recommend FinEdge have first-line oncall (Platform Eng + ML), Redwood provides a 24/7 on-call for infra and SE support during the scheduled window. We'll share the escalation matrix.
[07:41] Rachel: What about cost observation during ramp? We want alerts for spend burn so we can pause traffic if costs exceed forecast.
[07:48] Diego: We have budget alerts tied to token spend and node-hours. We'll add a forecast model for the canary and alert at configurable thresholds (50%, 80%, 100%).
[07:59] Priya: One more compliance item - we need the signed DPA and an answer on data residency for EU customers.
[08:06] Samira: We'll send the DPA and confirm region controls. For Dedicated in EU region, data residency can be enforced; we'll confirm the specific region endpoints. Diego will include the docs.
[08:19] Marcus: Small quirk we saw in yesterday's run: the KV cache not persisting across a hot restart which raised token counts. Is that expected?
[08:27] Diego: That shouldn't be typical - hot restart preserves cache if pinned. We'll investigate; may be a config in your test cluster. Add to action items: Diego to debug the restart behavior with Marcus.
[08:39] Samira: Noted. Diego, put that in the action list.
[08:42] Diego: Will do.
[08:45] Tom: On instrumentation - will Redwood emit trace IDs we can correlate with our internal tracing?
[08:50] Diego: Yes - we propagate trace IDs and include them in logs. We'll share the tracing spec.
[08:56] Rachel: For the A/B evaluation, can Redwood run the automated eval harness or do we run it locally?
[09:02] Diego: We can run it on your behalf or provide the harness. For the POC, we can run a parallel eval and share the results; for production you might ingest evaluations into your internal pipeline.
[09:14] Samira: Let's decide who runs the 24-hour benchmark - Diego can run an initial pass on Redwood side and then we'll hand it over.
[09:20] Diego: I'll schedule the 24h latency/cost run with the quantized model and share the logs + cost spreadsheet.
[09:26] Marcus: Any limitations we should be aware of in terms of rate limits or token caps during the canary?
[09:31] Diego: We'll set temporary elevated quotas for the canary and document them. If you need sustained higher throughput we recommend reserved nodes in Dedicated.
[09:42] Priya: For the SOC2 addendum and audit logs, can you list who the point of contact is on your side?
[09:47] Samira: I'm the primary contact for contracting and compliance, Diego is the technical contact for logs and KMS.
[09:52] Tom: Ok, let's capture final agreements so we can move to scheduling: 1) Redwood provides runbook + dashboards by 2026-10-04, 2) FinEdge shares endpoints & traffic patterns by 2026-10-06, 3) Diego runs 24h benchmark by 2026-10-05, 4) security sign-offs aimed by 2026-10-06, 5) tentative cutover weekend 2026-10-16.
[10:16] Samira: That matches our notes; we'll send a follow-up email with the timeline and calendar invites for the pre-cutover readiness call.
[10:25] Rachel: One last question - do you support gradual model parameter tweaks without a full redeploy (e.g., temperature, decode params)?
[10:33] Diego: Yes, we support config flags and can adjust decode params at the route level. Many teams use that for lightweight tuning before full model swap.
[10:41] Tom: Great. If no more questions, let's recap.
[10:45] Samira: Quick recap: runbook + dashboards by 10/04, Diego benchmark by 10/05, FinEdge to share traffic by 10/06, security sign-off 10/06, plan for canary mid-October. Action items captured.
[10:58] Rachel: Thanks everyone.
[11:00] Samira: Thanks all - we'll follow up.

End of transcript.

Notes: Transcript includes minor transcription artifacts; some technical nouns abbreviated. Refer to attached runbook draft and Grafana links that will be posted in follow-up email.
